requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed no pre-existing appworker user, then created it via useradd -m; id/getent both show uid=1001(appworker) with a home directory and shell, verified both before and after the restart.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile to 8192 for appworker, pam_limits.so is confirmed active in system-auth and password-auth, and an actual login shell (su - appworker) reports ulimit -n = 8192, both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 256 processes
requirements.summary: Same appworker.conf sets soft/hard nproc to 256; a login shell via su - appworker reports ulimit -u = 256, confirmed again after the restart.

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account and enforced 8,192 open-file / 256-process limits for its login sessions via limits.d, confirmed pam_limits wiring, and directly verified the enforced ulimits through an actual login shell (su -), both before and after independently running the mandated node-restart evidence protocol. Boot identity changed (151c4aa9... -> d407be00...) with a matching uptime reset, node1 became unreachable then reachable again, and the account plus its limits were re-verified intact post-reboot, giving a complete restart evidence chain. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations were found.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package-manager consistency around this change cannot be independently confirmed, though it is not material to this account/limits task.
Restart evidence, while thorough, is supplemental to this task's contract rather than a stated requirement, so its quality affects confidence but not the task-outcome scoring above.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: useradd -m for the account, one tee write of limits.d/appworker.conf, and the mandated shutdown -r now for the node-restart evidence protocol. Verification commands (id, getent, grep, su -c ulimit) are read-only. The reboot left a /tmp/reboot.log artifact (stdout/stderr redirect target for the backgrounded shutdown command) and refreshed systemd-private tmp dirs, both expected, low-risk byproducts of a legitimate reboot rather than unwanted residue. No failed services, no exposed ports beyond the pre-existing baseline (post-restart listening sockets match pre-restart ones after boot_id-based renaming), and no abandoned or conflicting configuration was found in the after-executor snapshot.
